This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed seeking enhancement of the award, dated 12/09/2022 passed in MCOP No.515 of 2017 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Special District Court),
Trichirappalli.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Special District Court),
Trichirappalli
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2.The facts in brief:-
On 06/04/2017 at about 10.30 am, the injured Gunasekaran was riding his two wheeler bearing registration No.TN-48-AC-6863 with the pillion rider his wife namely Saritha on the Trichy-Mannachanallur road.
At that time, the first respondent Lorry bearing registration No.TN-37-AR-6900 was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and hit the two wheeler.
As a result of which, both of them fell down, sustained injuries, Saritha and himself was taken to the Government Hospital, Trichy.
But Saritha without responding to the treatment died on 06/04/2017.
3.Over the occurrence, a case in Crime No.239 of 2017 was registered by the Kollidam Police Station.
Saritha was aged about 35 and was working as a Tailor and earning not less than Rs.500/- per day.
The husband and the children filed the petition claiming compensation amount of Rs.15,00,000/-.
Similarly, Gunasekaran filed a https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis separate petition for the injuries suffered by him in MCOP No.595 of 2017.
Both were heard together.

4.That was resisted by the Insurance Company namely the second respondent herein by filing counter stating that the occurrence took place because of the rash and negligent driving on the part of the rider of the two wheeler namely Gunasekaran.
Gunasekaran without minding the traffic drove the two wheeler in a rash and negligent manner and invited the accident.
Apart from that, he was not owning proper driving licence.
5.Before the tribunal, on the side of the claimants, one witness was examined and 10 documents were marked.
On the side of the Insurance Company, no oral and documentary evidence was adduced.

6.At the conclusion of the trial process, regarding the first aspect of negligence, the Tribunal recorded a finding to the effect that it occurred due to the rash and negligent driving on the part of the first respondent Lorry driver, on the basis of the evidence on record as well as in the manner of the occurrence said to have been taken place.
Against which, no appeal was preferred by the Insurance Company.

So regarding the manner of the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis occurrence,
the finding of fact recorded by the Tribunal requires no interference and accordingly, it is sustained.
7.Regarding the compensation amount only, this appeal has been preferred by the appellants, who are the claimants.
8.With regard to the compensation, the Tribunal fixed the age of the deceased as 35, on the basis of the entry made in the postmortem certificate.
There is no evidence on record to show the correct income of the deceased.

But however, it fixed the daily wager amount as Rs.200/- and fixed the Gunasekaran vs Pandiraj on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7768148/
2 notional income as Rs.6,000/- per month.
To that, 40% of the future prospects was added.
1/3rd was deducted towards personal and living expenses.
Multiplier 16 was taken and finally arrived the following figure by adding the customary heads.

Loss of Dependency Rs.10,75,200/-
Transport charges to the Rs. 10,000/-
 hospital  Loss of estate Rs. 10,000/-

Medical treatment Rs. 15,600/-
 expenses  Loss of consortium Rs. 35,000/-
 Filial consortium Rs. 70,000/-
Funeral expenses Rs. 10,000/-

Total Rs.12,10,200/-
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
9.The learned counsel appearing for the appellants would submit that taking Rs.200/- per day for assessing the dependency is very meagre.
10.The short point that arises in this appeal is whether the appellants/claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation.
It is not disputed that the deceased Saritha was aged 35 years at the time of accident and was a home maker.
11.According to the claimants, the deceased was a tailor by profession and was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
The Tribunal in absence of any evidence with regard to the income of the deceased fixed the notional income at Rs.6,000/- per month.
12.No doubt, there is no proof in support of the income of the deceased.
In any event, the deceased was a home maker and her value to her family cannot be undermined.

The contribution of the home maker is invaluable and so, in my considered view the assessment of notional income at Rs.6,000/-
by the Tribunal does not reflect the true value of the home maker.
Hence, I am of the considered view that a sum of Rs.10,000/- can be fixed as notional income of the deceased.

If 40% is added https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis towards future prospects I.e., Rs.4,000/- (Rs.10,000/- x 40/100),
the income would be Rs.14,000/- (Rs.10,000/- + Rs.4,000/-).
If deducted 1/3rd towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased, it comes to Rs.9,333/- (Rs.14,000  Rs.4667).
The Tribunal was right in applying multiplier 16.
Thus, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards loss of dependency is modified to Rs.17,91,936/- (Rs.9,333/- x 12 x 16).
In respect of other conventional amount, it requires enhancement.
13.The
recalculation of the award amount is indicated hereunder:-
